acceptanceCriteria.statement: On a narrow viewport (mobile portrait), the primary note-capture CTA is visible without scrolling on the landing route default state.
The landing route hero contains exactly one primary call-to-action element, with no competing secondary CTA in the same visual fold.
On the note-capture screen, the input field and save action are positioned so both are reachable by a thumb in a single-handed portrait grip on a standard mobile viewport.
Reaching the saved state on note-capture does not trigger a route change or full-page navigation; confirmation renders inline.
No screen in this design reproduces the named reference's wordmark, logo, exact marketing copy, unique illustrations, distinctive iconography, or specific branded palette values.
The saved-state confirmation is conveyed through both a text label and a visual cue, not through color alone.

accessibilityAndRecovery: Landing headline and sub-headline text maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast against their background.
The primary CTA on the landing route is reachable via keyboard navigation as an early focusable element.
Note-capture saved confirmation uses both a text label and a visual cue so color-blind users can perceive success.
If the save action fails on note-capture, drafted text persists on-screen and an inline error message appears rather than discarding the user's input.
Empty-state placeholder copy in the capture input clears immediately on first keystroke to prevent confusion with real content.
Focus outlines on the capture textarea remain visibly distinct from its resting border state for keyboard and switch-device users.
assumptions: The exact accent color, canvas color, and typography for Notewright are not specified in the brief and are treated as an open design decision independent of Notion's palette.

No specific corpus screenshot depicts a note-capture flow; the note-capture blueprint's mobile single-handed-grip and inline-save-confirmation rules are derived directly from the brief's stated mobileRules rather than from evidence, and their exact pixel layout is an assumption pending further design work.

The brief does not specify whether Notewright's landing route includes a persistent navigation bar; this design assumes a minimal or absent top nav on the landing route to keep the hero as the sole above-the-fold focus, consistent with the single-CTA hero pattern in the brief.
No inspected URLs were supplied for either required screen; inspectedUrls are left empty rather than invented, per the constraint against claiming unobserved content.

The specific interaction for transitioning from drafting to saved (e.g., explicit button tap vs. autosave) is not specified in the brief and is assumed to require an explicit user-triggered save action given the brief's emphasis on note-taking as a deliberate task.

principles: Reserve the single most saturated accent color for exactly one interactive element per screen — the primary CTA — so the note-capture entry is never ambiguous.
Keep the headline stack left-aligned with one sub-headline sentence and one CTA, avoiding a dual-CTA or feature-grid hero that would dilute the above-the-fold task.
Use borders and hairline dividers rather than drop shadows or neumorphic elevation to separate the capture card from the canvas, keeping the composition legible on narrow viewports.
Communicate the saved-note state through both a color cue and a text label so the confirmation is legible without relying on hue alone.

Avoid reproducing any named reference's proprietary palette, wordmark, or illustration style; all visual choices here are generic layout patterns sourced from the adaptable corpus evidence, not from the named reference itself.
globalDirection.summary: Notewright's landing route adapts only the generic left-aligned headline-stack pattern named in the brief (single headline, one-sentence sub-headline, single primary CTA) while rejecting Notion's monochrome palette, wordmark, and any distinctive iconography. Structural cues borrowed from the evidence corpus (single-accent focal color, labeled nav, border-not-shadow card separation) are used to keep the note-capture entry unmistakable above the fold, not to imitate the named reference's visual identity.

accessibility: Headline and sub-headline maintain a documented minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the canvas color.
The single CTA is reachable via keyboard tab order as the first focusable element after any skip-link.
failureAndRecovery: If the CTA fails to route (e.g., script load failure), the CTA renders as a plain anchor link to the note-capture route so the journey is not blocked by JavaScript failure.
mobileRules: Primary note-capture CTA remains reachable above the fold on narrow viewports by collapsing the hero vertical rhythm and keeping the CTA within the first viewport height.
screenBlueprints.summary: A left-aligned headline stack (product name, one-sentence sub-headline, single primary CTA) occupies the top of the viewport with no competing secondary CTA, so a first-time visitor understands Notewright's purpose and reaches note-capture within one glance and one tap.

accessibility: Saved confirmation is communicated through both a color change and a text label ('Saved') rather than color alone.
The capture textarea retains visible focus outline distinct from its border-only resting state.
failureAndRecovery: If save fails (e.g., network error), the drafting state persists with the user's text intact and an inline error label appears adjacent to the save action, avoiding silent data loss.
Empty-state placeholder text disappears immediately on first keystroke to avoid confusion with entered content.
mobileRules: Capture input remains usable in a single-handed portrait grip by keeping the text field and save action within the lower two-thirds of a standard mobile viewport.
Saved state confirms capture without navigating away, using an inline confirmation rather than a route change or modal.
screenBlueprints.summary: A single-column capture input dominates the viewport in empty and drafting states; saving surfaces a confirmation state inline without navigation, so the note-taker never loses place.

sourceDecisions.rationale: Restricting the accent color to exactly one primary action (the note-capture CTA) borrows the generic single-focal-point pattern documented across multiple corpus entries; it gives the landing route one unmistakable next step without adopting any reference's specific hue or branded palette.

The brief explicitly names the left-aligned headline-stack-plus-single-CTA layout as the safe generic pattern to adapt from the named reference's public marketing homepage; this is a structural convention (alignment, hierarchy, one CTA) rather than a proprietary asset.

Using hairline borders instead of elevation/shadow to separate the capture surface from the canvas keeps the composition flat and legible on narrow viewports, following the corpus pattern of border-based structure over neumorphic lift for content that must be scanned quickly.

Pairing the saved-state color cue with a text label follows the corpus convention of redundant color-plus-text status communication, which serves the brief's mobile rule that saved state must confirm capture without navigation and must be legible to users who cannot rely on color alone.

Avoiding a flanking secondary link next to the primary CTA reduces decision paralysis on the landing route, adapting the generic single-CTA-forces-a-binary-choice principle documented in the corpus rather than the reference's specific copy or button styling.

The brief explicitly forbids reproducing the named reference's branded monochrome palette (#FFFFFF/#000000) and specific typographic choices; Notewright must select its own canvas and accent colors independent of that identity.

The brief requires an explicit reject decision for any proprietary identifier drawn from the named reference; the Notion wordmark, logo, unique illustrations, and distinctive iconography are excluded from this design regardless of their popularity as a pattern source.

Icon-only navigation without text labels is rejected for the landing and note-capture routes because the brief's users include first-time visitors who need to understand the tool's purpose immediately; label-paired controls (where any nav exists) reduce learning cost, per corpus guidance on labeled versus icon-only navigation.
